title: Multiplication and Division Word Problems: Interpreting Remainders
seo_title: Grade 4 Multiplication and Division Word Problems: Remainders (TEKS 4.4H, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.4H solve with fluency one- and two-step problems involving multiplication and division, including interpreting remainders
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 word problem worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.4H: interpret remainders, times as many, find the smaller amount and one- and two-step multiplication and division problems. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: Read the question to decide what the remainder means.
key_sub: Round up when everyone needs a place, drop the remainder when only full groups count, or give the remainder when asked what is left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Multiply when you know the number of groups and the size of each group, or when one amount is times as many as another.
  • Divide when you know the total and need the size of each group or the number of groups.
  • A remainder depends on the question: round up when everyone needs a place, drop it when only full groups count, or give the remainder when the question asks how many are left.

Examples

Example

125 students, 8 per van. How many vans?

125 ÷ 8 = 15 R5

5 students still need a seat.

Answer: 16 vans

Example

A tree is 6 times as tall as a 9-foot fence. How tall is the tree?

6 × 9

Answer: 54 feet

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Ignoring a remainder when everyone needs a seatAdd one more group for the leftovers.
Rounding up when only full groups countIf a bracelet needs 8 beads, a partial bracelet does not count.
Adding for times as manyTimes as many means multiply.

faq.a: Solve with fluency one- and two-step problems involving multiplication and division, including interpreting remainders.

faq.q: What does interpreting a remainder mean?
faq.a: Deciding what the leftover amount means in the story: one more group, ignore it, or report it.

faq.q: How do I know whether to multiply or divide?
faq.a: If you need a total from equal groups or times as many, multiply. If you split a total, divide.

faq.q: Why are remainders tricky on the STAAR?
faq.a: The same division can have different answers depending on the question, so always reread what is asked.

sets.title: What to do with the remainder

items.q: A bakery made 1,636 cookies. It packs them in boxes of 6 and fills as many boxes as it can. How many cookies are not in a box?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 6, so start with 16. 16 ÷ 6 = 2, 2 × 6 = 12, 16 − 12 = 4. Bring down 3: 43 ÷ 6 = 7, 7 × 6 = 42, 43 − 42 = 1. Bring down 6: 16 ÷ 6 = 2, 2 × 6 = 12, 16 − 12 = 4. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 4. So 1,636 ÷ 6 = 272 R 4. Check: 272 × 6 + 4 = 1,636. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 4 cookies.

items.q: A bike club rode 438 miles in 3 days. They rode the same distance each day. How many miles did they ride each day?
items.e: Divide: 4 ÷ 3 = 1, 1 × 3 = 3, 4 − 3 = 1. Bring down 3: 13 ÷ 3 = 4, 4 × 3 = 12, 13 − 12 = 1. Bring down 8: 18 ÷ 3 = 6, 6 × 3 = 18, 18 − 18 = 0. So 438 ÷ 3 = 146. Check: 146 × 3 = 438. There is no remainder, so the answer is 146 miles.

items.q: Liam is putting 266 photos into an album. Each page holds 6 photos. How many pages does he need for all the photos?
items.e: Divide: 2 is less than 6, so start with 26. 26 ÷ 6 = 4, 4 × 6 = 24, 26 − 24 = 2. Bring down 6: 26 ÷ 6 = 4, 4 × 6 = 24, 26 − 24 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 266 ÷ 6 = 44 R 2. Check: 44 × 6 + 2 = 266. 44 pages are not enough: 2 photos still need a page. Add 1 more, so the answer is 45 pages.

items.q: A school raised $3,132 at a book fair. It shares the money equally among 6 classes. How much money does each class get?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 6, so start with 31. 31 ÷ 6 = 5, 5 × 6 = 30, 31 − 30 = 1. Bring down 3: 13 ÷ 6 = 2, 2 × 6 = 12, 13 − 12 = 1. Bring down 2: 12 ÷ 6 = 2, 2 × 6 = 12, 12 − 12 = 0. So 3,132 ÷ 6 = 522. Check: 522 × 6 = 3,132. There is no remainder, so the answer is $522.

items.q: There are 365 days in a year. How many full weeks are in a year?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 7, so start with 36. 36 ÷ 7 = 5, 5 × 7 = 35, 36 − 35 = 1. Bring down 5: 15 ÷ 7 = 2, 2 × 7 = 14, 15 − 14 = 1. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 1. So 365 ÷ 7 = 52 R 1. Check: 52 × 7 + 1 = 365. The 1 day left over is not enough to make another week, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 52 weeks.

items.q: A deck has 52 cards. Mateo deals as many cards as he can so that each of 5 players gets the same number. How many cards are left over?
items.e: Divide: 5 ÷ 5 = 1, 1 × 5 = 5, 5 − 5 = 0. Bring down 2: 2 ÷ 5 = 0, so write 0 in the quotient. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 52 ÷ 5 = 10 R 2. Check: 10 × 5 + 2 = 52. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 2 cards.

items.q: Zoe shares 65 stickers equally among 6 friends. Each friend gets as many as possible. How many stickers are left over?
items.e: Divide: 6 ÷ 6 = 1, 1 × 6 = 6, 6 − 6 = 0. Bring down 5: 5 ÷ 6 = 0, so write 0 in the quotient. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 5. So 65 ÷ 6 = 10 R 5. Check: 10 × 6 + 5 = 65. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 5 stickers.

items.q: There are 116 people waiting for a boat ride across a lake. The boat carries 9 people on each trip. How many trips does the boat need to make?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 9, so start with 11. 11 ÷ 9 = 1, 1 × 9 = 9, 11 − 9 = 2. Bring down 6: 26 ÷ 9 = 2, 2 × 9 = 18, 26 − 18 = 8. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 8. So 116 ÷ 9 = 12 R 8. Check: 12 × 9 + 8 = 116. 12 trips are not enough: 8 people still need a ride. Add 1 more, so the answer is 13 trips.

items.q: Diego has a ribbon that is 155 inches long. He cuts it into pieces that are each 6 inches long. How many pieces can he cut?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 6, so start with 15. 15 ÷ 6 = 2, 2 × 6 = 12, 15 − 12 = 3. Bring down 5: 35 ÷ 6 = 5, 5 × 6 = 30, 35 − 30 = 5. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 5. So 155 ÷ 6 = 25 R 5. Check: 25 × 6 + 5 = 155. The 5 inches left over are not enough to cut another piece, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 25 pieces.

items.q: A factory has 3,123 crayons. It puts 8 crayons in each box. How many boxes can it fill completely?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 8, so start with 31. 31 ÷ 8 = 3, 3 × 8 = 24, 31 − 24 = 7. Bring down 2: 72 ÷ 8 = 9, 9 × 8 = 72, 72 − 72 = 0. Bring down 3: 3 ÷ 8 = 0, so write 0 in the quotient. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 3. So 3,123 ÷ 8 = 390 R 3. Check: 390 × 8 + 3 = 3,123. The 3 crayons left over are not enough to fill another box, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 390 boxes.

items.q: There are 237 guests at a wedding. Each table seats 8 guests. How many tables are needed so every guest has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 2 is less than 8, so start with 23. 23 ÷ 8 = 2, 2 × 8 = 16, 23 − 16 = 7. Bring down 7: 77 ÷ 8 = 9, 9 × 8 = 72, 77 − 72 = 5. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 5. So 237 ÷ 8 = 29 R 5. Check: 29 × 8 + 5 = 237. 29 tables are not enough: 5 guests still need a seat. Add 1 more, so the answer is 30 tables.

items.q: Aaliyah has 116 beads. She makes bracelets with 6 beads each and says she can make 19 bracelets with 2 beads left over. Which expression checks her answer? It should equal 116.
items.e: Multiply the number of bracelets by the beads on each one, then add the beads left over: 6 × 19 = 114, 114 + 2 = 116. That is all 116 beads, so her answer is right.

items.q: A farm collected 1,310 eggs. Each carton holds 6 eggs. How many cartons are needed to hold all the eggs?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 6, so start with 13. 13 ÷ 6 = 2, 2 × 6 = 12, 13 − 12 = 1. Bring down 1: 11 ÷ 6 = 1, 1 × 6 = 6, 11 − 6 = 5. Bring down 0: 50 ÷ 6 = 8, 8 × 6 = 48, 50 − 48 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 1,310 ÷ 6 = 218 R 2. Check: 218 × 6 + 2 = 1,310. 218 cartons are not enough: 2 eggs still need a carton. Add 1 more, so the answer is 219 cartons.

items.q: Ms. Lee has 139 pencils. She puts the same number of pencils in each of 7 cups, as many as she can. How many pencils are left over?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 7, so start with 13. 13 ÷ 7 = 1, 1 × 7 = 7, 13 − 7 = 6. Bring down 9: 69 ÷ 7 = 9, 9 × 7 = 63, 69 − 63 = 6. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 6. So 139 ÷ 7 = 19 R 6. Check: 19 × 7 + 6 = 139. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 6 pencils.

items.q: Camila has $65. Movie tickets cost $9 each. How many tickets can she buy?
items.e: Divide: 6 is less than 9, so start with 65. 65 ÷ 9 = 7, 7 × 9 = 63, 65 − 63 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 65 ÷ 9 = 7 R 2. Check: 7 × 9 + 2 = 65. The 2 dollars left over are not enough to buy another ticket, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 7 tickets.

items.q: An orchard picked 1,198 apples. The apples are packed in bags of 8. How many full bags can be packed?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 8, so start with 11. 11 ÷ 8 = 1, 1 × 8 = 8, 11 − 8 = 3. Bring down 9: 39 ÷ 8 = 4, 4 × 8 = 32, 39 − 32 = 7. Bring down 8: 78 ÷ 8 = 9, 9 × 8 = 72, 78 − 72 = 6. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 6. So 1,198 ÷ 8 = 149 R 6. Check: 149 × 8 + 6 = 1,198. The 6 apples left over are not enough to fill another bag, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 149 bags.

items.q: A total of 104 students sign up for a soccer tournament. Each team needs 7 players. How many full teams can be made?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 7, so start with 10. 10 ÷ 7 = 1, 1 × 7 = 7, 10 − 7 = 3. Bring down 4: 34 ÷ 7 = 4, 4 × 7 = 28, 34 − 28 = 6. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 6. So 104 ÷ 7 = 14 R 6. Check: 14 × 7 + 6 = 104. The 6 students left over are not enough to make another team, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 14 teams.

items.q: A school is taking 172 students and adults on a field trip. Each van holds 7 people. How many vans are needed to take everyone?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 7, so start with 17. 17 ÷ 7 = 2, 2 × 7 = 14, 17 − 14 = 3. Bring down 2: 32 ÷ 7 = 4, 4 × 7 = 28, 32 − 28 = 4. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 4. So 172 ÷ 7 = 24 R 4. Check: 24 × 7 + 4 = 172. 24 vans are not enough: 4 people still need a van. Add 1 more, so the answer is 25 vans.

items.q: There are 75 campers going on an overnight trip. Each tent sleeps 6 campers. How many tents are needed?
items.e: Divide: 7 ÷ 6 = 1, 1 × 6 = 6, 7 − 6 = 1. Bring down 5: 15 ÷ 6 = 2, 2 × 6 = 12, 15 − 12 = 3. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 3. So 75 ÷ 6 = 12 R 3. Check: 12 × 6 + 3 = 75. 12 tents are not enough: 3 campers still need a tent. Add 1 more, so the answer is 13 tents.

items.q: A school library is moving 1,878 books. Each box holds 9 books. How many boxes are needed to pack all the books?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 9, so start with 18. 18 ÷ 9 = 2, 2 × 9 = 18, 18 − 18 = 0. Bring down 7: 7 ÷ 9 = 0, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 8: 78 ÷ 9 = 8, 8 × 9 = 72, 78 − 72 = 6. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 6. So 1,878 ÷ 9 = 208 R 6. Check: 208 × 9 + 6 = 1,878. 208 boxes are not enough: 6 books still need a box. Add 1 more, so the answer is 209 boxes.

sets.title: Find the smaller amount or how many times: divide

items.q: Jayden has 300 stickers. Caleb has 50 stickers. How many times as many stickers as Caleb does Jayden have?
items.e: To find “how many times”, divide the bigger amount by the smaller one. Think: ☐ × 50 = 300. 6 × 50 = 300, so the answer is 6. 300 − 50 = 250 tells how many more, not how many times.

items.q: An orchard has 300 apple trees and 75 pear trees. How many times as many apple trees as pear trees does it have?
items.e: To find “how many times”, divide the bigger amount by the smaller one. Think: ☐ × 75 = 300. 4 × 75 = 300, so the answer is 4. 300 − 75 = 225 tells how many more, not how many times.

items.q: Nevaeh scored 1,230 points in a video game. That is 5 times as many points as Ethan scored. How many points did Ethan score?
items.e: The bigger amount, 1,230, is 5 equal parts. Each part is the smaller amount, so divide: 1,230 ÷ 5 = 246. Check: 5 × 246 = 1,230. Answer: 246 points.

items.q: The big tank at a pet store has 168 fish. That is 7 times as many fish as the small tank has. How many fish are in the small tank?

items.q: A city has 8,000 people, and a nearby town has 2,000 people. How many times as many people as the town does the city have?

items.q: A blue ribbon is 75 inches long, and a red ribbon is 15 inches long. How many times as long as the red ribbon is the blue ribbon?
items.e: To find “how many times”, divide the bigger amount by the smaller one. Think: ☐ × 15 = 75. 5 × 15 = 75, so the answer is 5. 75 − 15 = 60 tells how many more, not how many times.

items.q: A blue whale is 88 feet long. It is 8 times as long as a dolphin. How long is the dolphin?
items.e: The bigger amount, 88, is 8 equal parts. Each part is the smaller amount, so divide: 88 ÷ 8 = 11. Check: 8 × 11 = 88. Answer: 11 feet.

items.q: A farm has 315 chickens. That is 7 times as many chickens as cows. How many cows does the farm have?
items.e: The bigger amount, 315, is 7 equal parts. Each part is the smaller amount, so divide: 315 ÷ 7 = 45. Check: 7 × 45 = 315. Answer: 45 cows.

sets.title: Times as many or how many more?

items.q: Zoe has 24 toy cars. Ximena has 4 times as many toy cars as Zoe. How many toy cars does Ximena have?
items.e: “4 times as many” means 4 groups of 24: 4 × 24 = 96. Adding (24 + 4 = 28) would answer “4 more”. Answer: 96 toy cars.

items.q: Caleb has 15 marbles. Nevaeh has 8 times as many marbles as Caleb. How many marbles does Nevaeh have?
items.e: “8 times as many” means 8 groups of 15: 8 × 15 = 120. Adding (15 + 8 = 23) would answer “8 more”. Answer: 120 marbles.

items.q: Camila biked 18 miles this month. Carlos biked 8 times as far as Camila. How much farther did Carlos bike than Camila?
items.e: Step 1: find the bigger amount: 8 × 18 = 144. Step 2: “how many more” means subtract: 144 − 18 = 126. 144 is the bigger amount, not the difference. Answer: 126 miles.

items.q: Josiah has 19 stamps. Emma has 8 times as many stamps as Josiah. How many stamps does Emma have?
items.e: “8 times as many” means 8 groups of 19: 8 × 19 = 152. Adding (19 + 8 = 27) would answer “8 more”. Answer: 152 stamps.

items.q: Sofia has 14 comic books. Liam has 8 times as many comic books as Sofia. How many more comic books does Liam have than Sofia?
items.e: Step 1: find the bigger amount: 8 × 14 = 112. Step 2: “how many more” means subtract: 112 − 14 = 98. 112 is the bigger amount, not the difference. Answer: 98 comic books.

items.q: A school bus is 40 feet long. A car is 8 feet long. Which sentence is true?
c: The bus is 5 feet longer than the car
The bus is 32 times as long as the car
The bus is 5 times as long as the car
The car is 5 times as long as the bus
items.e: 5 × 8 = 40, so the bus is 5 times as long as the car. It is 40 − 8 = 32 feet longer, not 5 feet longer.

items.q: Harper has 18 shells. Elijah has 3 more shells than Harper. How many shells does Elijah have?
items.e: “3 more” means add 3: 18 + 3 = 21. Multiplying (3 × 18 = 54) would answer a “3 times as …” question. Answer: 21 shells.

items.q: Sofia has 25 comic books. Liam has 9 more comic books than Sofia. How many comic books does Liam have?
items.e: “9 more” means add 9: 25 + 9 = 34. Multiplying (9 × 25 = 225) would answer a “9 times as …” question. Answer: 34 comic books.

items.q: Gabriel has 25 baseball cards. Marcus has 5 times as many baseball cards as Gabriel. How many baseball cards does Marcus have?
items.e: “5 times as many” means 5 groups of 25: 5 × 25 = 125. Adding (25 + 5 = 30) would answer “5 more”. Answer: 125 baseball cards.

items.q: Luis has 22 seashells. Valeria has 8 times as many seashells as Luis. How many more seashells does Valeria have than Luis?
items.e: Step 1: find the bigger amount: 8 × 22 = 176. Step 2: “how many more” means subtract: 176 − 22 = 154. 176 is the bigger amount, not the difference. Answer: 154 seashells.

items.q: Ethan made a paper chain 24 inches long. Grace made a chain 8 inches longer than Ethan's chain. How long is Grace's chain?
items.e: “8 inches longer” means add 8: 24 + 8 = 32. Multiplying (8 × 24 = 192) would answer a “8 times as …” question. Answer: 32 inches.

items.q: Lucia has 13 stickers. Mia has 4 more stickers than Lucia. Which equation finds a, the number of stickers Mia has?
items.e: “4 more than 13” means add: a = 13 + 4 = 17. “4 times as many” would be a = 4 × 13.

items.q: Lucia has 16 crayons. Mia has 9 more crayons than Lucia. How many crayons does Mia have?
items.e: “9 more” means add 9: 16 + 9 = 25. Multiplying (9 × 16 = 144) would answer a “9 times as …” question. Answer: 25 crayons.

items.q: Mateo has 17 beads. Isaac has 8 times as many beads as Mateo. How many beads does Isaac have?
items.e: “8 times as many” means 8 groups of 17: 8 × 17 = 136. Adding (17 + 8 = 25) would answer “8 more”. Answer: 136 beads.

items.q: A book costs $19. A video game costs 5 times as much as the book. How much does the video game cost?
items.e: “5 times as much” means 5 groups of 19: 5 × 19 = 95. Adding (19 + 5 = 24) would answer “5 more”. Answer: $95.

items.q: A small fish tank holds 6 gallons. A big tank holds 8 more gallons than the small tank. How many gallons does the big tank hold?
items.e: “8 more” means add 8: 6 + 8 = 14. Multiplying (8 × 6 = 48) would answer a “8 times as …” question. Answer: 14 gallons.

items.q: Noah has 21 rocks. Ava has 7 more rocks than Noah. How many rocks does Ava have?
items.e: “7 more” means add 7: 21 + 7 = 28. Multiplying (7 × 21 = 147) would answer a “7 times as …” question. Answer: 28 rocks.

items.q: Harper picked 12 strawberries. Elijah picked 4 times as many strawberries as Harper. Which equation finds p, the number Elijah picked?
items.e: “4 times as many as 12” means multiply: p = 4 × 12 = 48. “4 more” would be p = 12 + 4.

items.q: Noah has 15 rocks. Ava has 5 times as many rocks as Noah. How many more rocks does Ava have than Noah?
items.e: Step 1: find the bigger amount: 5 × 15 = 75. Step 2: “how many more” means subtract: 75 − 15 = 60. 75 is the bigger amount, not the difference. Answer: 60 rocks.

items.q: Ethan picked 42 apples. Grace picked 6 apples. Which sentence is true?
c: Ethan picked 7 more apples than Grace
Ethan picked 36 times as many apples as Grace
Grace picked 36 more apples than Ethan
Ethan picked 36 more apples than Grace
items.e: 42 − 6 = 36, so Ethan picked 36 more. Ethan also picked 7 times as many (7 × 6 = 42), but not 7 more.
